title: Renunciation
note: This means letting go of attachment to outer wealth and to the inner body, on seeing that neither lasts. That is also why it follows impermanence.

couplets.plain: From each thing you have let go of, you suffer no more pain.
couplets.pm: From each thing you have renounced, you suffer no pain. The pain is of two kinds: in this life, from seeking, guarding and losing it, and in the next, from sin. Giving up everything at once is best, but even giving things up one by one frees you from the pain they bring.

links.quote: From each thing you have let go of, you suffer no more pain
links.reason: Promises relief item by item: each thing given up takes its own pain with it.

links.quote: each thing you have let go of

couplets.plain: If you want them, renounce while you can. Once you have renounced, many things are yours here.
couplets.pm: If you renounce everything, many joys are yours in this very life. If you want them, renounce in good time. They come from mind, speech and body no longer being driven about by things, and from moving on the good path. Whoever renounces in youth has them longest. So renouncing brings joys, not only freedom from pain.
couplets.note: He supplies “joys” and “time”. The Tamil names neither.

links.quote: Once you have renounced, many things are yours here
links.reason: Reverses the expected loss: renouncing brings many things here, rather than taking them away.
Adds urgency for one already feeling the pull: if you want what it brings, go while you can.

couplets.plain: You must crush the hold of the five senses and give up, all together, everything you wanted.
couplets.pm: Those seeking release must crush the enjoyment of the five senses, and in doing so give up, all at once, everything they gathered to enjoy. That enjoyment drives the mind towards things won only by pain and sin, away from yoga and wisdom. Fed with such things it flares up like fire given firewood, and can’t be crushed.

links.quote: crush the hold of the five senses
give up, all together, everything you wanted
links.reason: Asks for more than the senses: everything you wanted is to go, all together.

couplets.plain: Having nothing at all is the way of penance. Owning even one thing brings back delusion.
couplets.pm: Having nothing to cling to is natural to those who do penance. Owning even one thing drives the penance away and becomes a cause of delusion again. If you give up all but one thing, everything you gave up comes back through it, breaks your penance and troubles your mind.

links.quote: Having nothing at all is the way of penance
Owning even one thing brings back delusion
links.reason: Speaks of one doing penance, warning that owning a single thing brings back delusion.

couplets.plain: For those out to cut off birth, even the body is too much. Why then any other ties?
couplets.pm: For those set on cutting off birth, even the body, their tool for it, is surplus. Then why have any further ties? “Body” means both the visible one and the subtle one, the mind joined with the senses, the vital airs and the results of desire and deeds. Seeing the constant suffering of these, they can’t bear the bond a moment and hurry to release.

links.quote: even the body is too much

couplets.plain: Whoever cuts away the pride that says “I” and “mine” will enter a world higher than the gods’.
couplets.pm: Whoever destroys the delusion that calls the body “I” and unrelated things “mine” reaches the world of release, hard even for the gods to reach. Destroying it means seeing, through a teacher’s words and the practice of yoga, that these are neither I nor mine, and letting go. Release is only for those who give up both kinds of attachment.

links.reason: Traces pride to the very words “I” and “mine”, and promises a higher world for cutting it away.

couplets.plain: Suffering holds on and won’t let go of those who hold on to attachment and won’t let go.
couplets.pm: Those who grip both kinds of attachment and won’t let go are gripped by the sufferings of birth, which won’t let them go. Gripping means loving fiercely. So those who don’t let go have no release.

links.quote: hold on to attachment and won’t let go
links.reason: Mirrors clinging with its punishment: they won’t let go, and suffering won’t let go of them.

couplets.plain: Those who renounce completely have arrived. All others are deluded, and caught in a net.
couplets.pm: Those who renounce completely have reached release. To renounce completely is to sicken of all things and of both bodies, and to let them go with no attachment. Those who don’t, who keep even a little attachment to any of these, have been deluded by false paths and caught in the net of birth.

links.quote: Those who renounce completely have arrived
links.reason: Allows no middle ground: complete renouncing arrives, and all others sit in a net.

couplets.plain: The moment attachment ends, birth is cut off. Otherwise you will see impermanence.
couplets.pm: The moment both kinds of attachment are gone, their ending cuts off birth. While they remain, you see the impermanence of being born and dying through them. When a cause goes, its effect goes at once.

links.reason: Says that without ending attachment you go on seeing impermanence.

links.quote: The moment attachment ends, birth is cut off
links.reason: Fixes the exact moment of freedom: birth is cut off the instant attachment ends.

couplets.plain: Hold to the attachment of the one who has no attachment. Hold to that attachment, so that you can let go of attachment.
couplets.pm: God holds all things yet is free of attachment. Take the path to release that god taught as the good path, and hold it in your mind. Then with that mind practise its means, meditation and absorption, to let go of the attachment to the body that has come with you from no beginning.

links.quote: Hold to the attachment of the one who has no attachment
links.reason: Bids the seeker hold to the one who has no attachment.

links.quote: so that you can let go of attachment
links.reason: Makes letting go of attachment the reason for holding to that one.

links.remove: The ark isn’t in the Tamil, which says only hold.

ideaLinks.quote: Suffering holds on and won’t let go
ideaLinks.reason: Suffering seizes whoever won’t give up attachment, and it doesn’t let go.
Each thing you give up ends the pain that came from it.

ideaLinks.quote: Those who renounce completely have arrived
ideaLinks.reason: Those who renounce completely have reached the goal, while the rest stay in the net.

ideaLinks.quote: The moment attachment ends, birth is cut off
ideaLinks.reason: Birth is cut off the moment attachment ends, so it is attachment that keeps births coming.

ideaLinks.quote: so that you can let go of attachment
ideaLinks.reason: Holding to the one who has no attachment is how you let go of your own.
